20-001.r: Union Territories → 7 when asked; now 8: Delhi, Chandigarh, Lakshadweep, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu, Puducherry, A&N Islands, J&K, Ladakh (with 28 states).

20-002.r: Largest UT among the options → Delhi (1483 sq km) > Puducherry (490) > Chandigarh (114) > Daman and Diu (111); Delhi is also the most populous UT.

20-003.r: Smallest UT → Lakshadweep (32 sq km; population 64473); largest UT by area (as of 26 January 2020) → Ladakh.

20-004.r: Puducherry UT → four districts: Puducherry and Karaikal (in Tamil Nadu), Mahe (in Kerala), Yanam (in Andhra Pradesh).

20-005.r: Tripura → a State, not a UT (Bangladesh on three sides); Daman and Diu, Lakshadweep and Puducherry → UTs.

20-006.r: Daman and Diu → capital Daman; Gulf of Khambhat lies between Daman and Diu; ruled by the Portuguese (not the British) after independence.

20-007.r: Map UT → Dadra and Nagar Haveli (now merged with Daman and Diu), capital Silvassa; Dadra is surrounded by Gujarat, Nagar Haveli on the Maharashtra–Gujarat border.

20-009.r: Goa → a State (smallest by area), not a UT; Lakshadweep, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Chandigarh → UTs.

20-010.r: NCR → all of NCT Delhi plus districts of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan; Madhya Pradesh is not part of it.

21-001.r: Jarawas → Andaman and Nicobar; Kukkis → Manipur; Tharus → Uttar Pradesh (Terai); Gonds → Madhya Pradesh.

21-002.r: Yellow skin, oblique eyes, high cheekbones, sparse straight hair → Mongoloids (north-east and south-east Asia).

21-003.r: Racial group of the hilly, forested north-east of India → Mongoloids.

21-004.r: Proto-Australoid (pre-Dravidian) race → Santhal, Bhil and Yeruva tribes.

21-005.r: Dravidian races → mainly South India (also central and south-east India); linked to Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Telugu languages.

21-006.r: Only anthropoid ape in India → White-browed gibbon of Assam (north-east India).

21-007.r: No notified tribal community (Census 2011) → Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh, NCT of Delhi and Puducherry.

21-008.r: Correct pair: Tharu–Uttarakhand (also UP, Bihar). Bhutia → Sikkim, West Bengal; Kol → MP, Chhattisgarh and others; Munda → mainly Jharkhand.

21-009.r: Tharus (Khatima and Sitarganj in Udham Singh Nagar; Terai of UP and Bihar) → follow Hinduism but observe Diwali as a festival of mourning.

21-012.r: Tharu tribe → Uttarakhand (largest tribe there), Uttar Pradesh (third, after Gond and Kharwar) and Bihar (third, after Santhal and Gond).

21-014.r: Correct: Limboo → Sikkim; Dongaria Kondh → Odisha. Wrong: Karbi → Assam (not Himachal); Bonda → Odisha (not Tamil Nadu).

21-015.r: Gaddi → main tribe of the Dhauladhar Range (Kangra and Chamba, Himachal Pradesh; also J&K); population about 1.5 lakh.

21-017.r: Odd pair: Kalahari–America; the Kalahari is in Africa (Botswana, Namibia, South Africa). Correct: Gobi–Mongolia; Thar–India; Sahara–Africa.

21-018.r: Santhals → Eastern India (West Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Tripura); 'Santhals–Chhattisgarh' is a wrong pair.

21-020.r: Santhal marriage → Bupla (Sanga, Kirin, Itut, Nir Bolok types); bride price 'Pon'; 'Bitlaha' → severe social boycott.

21-021.r: Transhumance (migratory pastoralism) → Bhotias (Mongoloid; hills of Uttarakhand); Bhoksas, Jaunsaris and Tharus are settled farmers.

21-022.r: Bodos → mainly Assam (Bodoland); the exam answer 'Garo hills' is only the nearest option. Santhal Pargana is a Santhal-majority division of Jharkhand.
21-022.c: The book says Bodos live mainly in the Garo hills of Meghalaya; they live mainly in Assam (Bodoland). Garo hills is only the nearest option.

21-023.r: Garo tribe → Meghalaya, Assam, Nagaland, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram, so one option cannot be picked. The book gives no single answer (*).

21-024.r: Khasi and Garo speakers → mainly Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram, so one option cannot be picked. The book gives no single answer (*).

21-025.r: None is a Kerala tribe: Chenchu → Nallamala (Andhra–Telangana); Lepcha → Sikkim; Dafla → Arunachal; Dafar → Saurashtra (Gujarat). The book gives no single answer (*).

21-026.r: Largest tribe of India (Census 2011) → Bhil (17071049); Gond (13256928) is second; Gond was largest when first asked.

21-029.r: Bhil is India's largest tribe but is not an option, so Gond is the answer among Gond, Irula, Panian, Raji.

21-030.r: Toda tribe (Todi, Tuda) → Nilgiri Hills; claim descent from Aryans; their language is Toda.

21-032.r: Ho tribe marriages → 'Andi' (by negotiation) and 'Oportipi' (by capture).

21-033.r: Polyandry → practised by the Toda tribe.

21-034.r: Sarhul festival (tree worship; Chaitra to Jeth, marks the new year) → Oraon, Munda, Santhal and Ho tribes of Jharkhand.

21-035.r: Sarhul → celebrated by Munda, Ho, Santhal and Oraon tribes of Jharkhand, so both Santhal and Munda fit. The book gives no single answer (*).

21-036.r: Ghumkaria → youth dormitory of the Oraon tribe; Oraon village chief 'Mahato', panchayat 'Panchora'.

21-037.r: Largest ST of Uttarakhand (Census 2011) → Tharu (91,342) > Jaunsari (88,664) > Bhoksa (54,037) > Bhotia (39,106) > Raji (690); Jaunsari led when asked.

21-038.r: Mizoram settlements → linear along ridges, because the valleys are cooler (especially at night) than the ridges.

21-039.r: All pairs correct (Census 2011): Bhotia → UP (5196); Khasi → Meghalaya; Santhal → Jharkhand; Toda → Tamil Nadu (2002). The book gives no single answer (*).

21-041.r: Wrong pair: Onam–Andhra Pradesh; Onam is Kerala's festival. Correct: Bihu → Assam; Pongal → Tamil Nadu; Baisakhi → Punjab.

21-042.r: Wrong pair: Sikkim–Tibetan; Sikkim's main languages are Nepali, Bhutia and Lepcha. Correct: Goa → Konkani; Meghalaya → Khasi; Nagaland → Angami.

21-043.r: All pairs correct (Census 2011): Angami → Nagaland; Apatani → Arunachal; Bhotiya → UP, Uttarakhand; Gonds → MP. The book gives no single answer (*).
21-043.t: Don't confuse Bhotiya (UP, Uttarakhand) with Bhutiya (Sikkim, Tripura, West Bengal).

21-044.r: Bhil (from 'villu/billu' = bow; Proto-Australoid) → MP, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan, also Tripura; famous dance Ghoomar.

21-045.r: Polyandry in India → Jaunsari, Khas, Toda, Kota, Bota, Tian, Irawa, Nayar; not Gonds or Nagas.

21-046.r: Bhil → Rajasthan; Santhal → Jharkhand; Raji → Uttarakhand; Lepcha → Sikkim.

21-047.r: Birhor → Jharkhand; Bhutia → Sikkim; Toda → Tamil Nadu; Sentinelese → Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

21-048.r: Toda → Tamil Nadu; Lepcha → Sikkim; Birhor → Jharkhand; Garo → Meghalaya.

21-049.r: Tharu → Uttar Pradesh; Bhil → Rajasthan; Gaddi → Himachal Pradesh; Munda → Jharkhand.

21-050.r: Jarawa → Andaman and Nicobar Islands; Munda → Jharkhand; Bhil → Rajasthan; Gaddi → Himachal Pradesh.

21-051.r: Sahariya → a main tribe of Rajasthan (name from Arabic 'Sehara', wilderness); in the news for starvation deaths.

21-052.r: Jaunsari → Uttarakhand; Santhal → Jharkhand; Bhil → Madhya Pradesh; Lepcha → Sikkim.

21-053.r: Basis for identifying tribes in India → cultural specification and distinct habitation (primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical location).

21-054.r: Pahadi Korba → Jashpur; Baiga → Mandala; Maria → Patalkot (Chhindwara); Sehariya → Gwalior.

21-055.r: Moplah → Kerala; Murias → Chhattisgarh; Todas → Tamil Nadu; Mundas → Odisha.

21-057.r: Wrong: North-East holds over half of India's tribals (only 11.90%, Census 2011). True: Constitution has no ST definition (Arts 342, 366(25)); Todas → Nilgiris; Lotha → Nagaland language.

21-058.r: Not a middle-Indian tribe → Kadar (Kerala, Tamil Nadu); Baiga, Muria and Kharia are central Indian tribes.

21-059.r: Changpa → semi-nomadic Tibetan herders of Ladakh (Zaskar), not Uttarakhand; rear Pashmina goats; Scheduled Tribe since 1989. Statements 2 and 3 correct.

21-060.r: Not matched: Korba–Kodagu (Korba/Korwa live in Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh; Kodagu is in Karnataka). Kol and Munda are not primitive tribes. The book gives no single answer (*).

21-061.r: Wrong pair: Madhya Pradesh–Lambada; Lambadas came via Rajasthan to Andhra, Telangana, Odisha, Karnataka, Maharashtra. Correct: Assam–Miri; Nagaland–Konyak; Arunachal–Apatani.

21-062.r: Wrong pair: Zulu–Odisha; the Zulu are a South African tribe. Correct: Sherpa → Nepal; Tharu → Uttarakhand; Toda → South India.

21-063.r: Chhindwara → Bharia; Mandala → Gond; Jhabua → Bhil; Shivpuri → Sahariya.

21-064.r: Not native to Andaman and Nicobar → Rengma, a Naga tribe of Nagaland and Assam; Halchu, Onge and Shompen are island tribes.

21-065.r: Onge tribe → west of Little Andaman Island, Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

21-067.r: Jarawa tribe → South and Middle Andaman (A&N Islands); in the news when a court banned tourists in Jarawa areas.

21-070.r: Most primitive tribe of India → Jarawa (Andaman and Nicobar Islands).

21-071.r: Manganiyars → Muslim community of the Rajasthan desert (also Tharparkar and Sanghar in Sindh), known for the musical tradition of North-West India.

21-072.r: Primitive tribe → Korwa; Jharkhand's 9 primitive groups: Asur, Birhor, Birajia, Korwa, Pahadi Khariya, Parahiya, Sabar, Mal Pahariya, Souriya Pahariya.

21-073.r: Jhooming (jhum, shifting cultivation) → practised by the Khasis (Meghalaya) among the options.

21-074.r: Catechu ('Khair') makers → Khairwar tribe, named after it.

21-075.r: Santhals → Jharkhand; Bhil → Rajasthan; Toda → Tamil Nadu; Jarawas → Andaman and Nicobar.

21-076.r: 'Kudukh' (a Dravidian dialect) → spoken by the Oraon tribe.

21-078.r: Gaddis → Himachal Pradesh; Todas → Tamil Nadu; Khasis → Meghalaya; Naga → Manipur.

21-079.r: 'Lal Bangala' (kitchen) → Bhunjia tribe (Odisha; Proto-Australoid; speak a mixed Baiga–Chhattisgarhi dialect).

21-080.r: Bamboo-based livelihood (basket making) → Kamar tribe; endogamous, patrilineal and patrilocal.
